ai_show_review.summary: Epic Mountains > Dark Star > Eleven suite with soaring guitars and tight drums
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers a marathon second‑set centerpiece—Mountains Of The Moon into Dark Star, Saint Stephen and The Eleven—that crackles with high‑octane improvisation. Jerry’s lead work is blistering, Phil’s bass anchors the jams, and Tom Constanten’s organ adds rich texture. Overall soundboard sources capture the performance well despite minor tape quirks.
ai_show_review.review: The Ark hosts a memorable performance on April 22, 1969, where the Dead launch into a blistering first set before unleashing one of their most electrifying second‑set marathons. The Mountains Of The Moon → Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven sequence is the night’s crown jewel: Jerry Garcia’s feedback‑laden leads fry your brain, Phil Lesh drops bass “bombs” that drive the groove, and both Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart weave a tight, stereo‑rich drumming tapestry. Tom Constanten’s organ shines throughout, especially in The Other One and the extended jams, while Bob Weir lays down solid rhythm and adds vocal color on Dupree’s Diamond Blues. Though the Miller soundboard capture suffers from tape flips and occasional mix imbalances, it remains the most complete document of this high‑energy show, preserving every twist of the marathon improvisations.

best_recording.reason: Most complete source with the full Mountains‑Dark Star‑Eleven suite despite minor tape quirks; captures the band's peak energy.

band_performance.Phil: Lesh delivers bomb‑like bass lines that lock into the groove even when low in the mix; his vocal contributions add depth.
band_performance.Bob: Weir provides solid rhythm guitar foundation and adds vocal harmonies on Dupree's Diamond Blues, keeping the band grounded.
band_performance.Tom: Constanden’s organ is prominent and well‑balanced, enriching the texture of The Other One and the extended improvisations.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart delivers tight, energetic drumming with standout rolls around 24–25 min, contributing to the show’s momentum.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann’s crisp cymbal work and driving beats complement Hart, creating a powerful stereo drum picture.
